title: POC deployment playbook - Galaxy Insurance scoping
summary: Discovery + POC scoping focused on deployment-mode decision (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer cares about throughput for underwriting inference (~200-400 req/min peak), P95 latency <350ms for short prompts, strict data residency and SOC2/PCI-ish controls, and a 6 week pilot timeline with benchmarks on a representative policy-annotation workload.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-08 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya(Patel) Redwood AE, Carlos Vega Redwood SE, Zoe Kim Redwood Solutions, Liam Chen VP Eng (Galaxy), Priya Rao Head of MLOps, Ava Mitchell Security, Tom Brooks SRE.

Summary/Context: quick intro then deep dive into deployment choices and concrete POC success criteria.

00:00:03 - Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round the room?
00:00:12 - Liam (Customer): yeah Liam here, I'll kick off — we run the claims/underwriting pipelines, we've got a new feature to auto-annotate policy text, need very predictable latency.
00:00:22 - Priya (Customer): Priya — MLOps. we'll own the pilot, want to know what infra you need and what we have to provide.
00:00:28 - Ava (Customer): Ava — security. I'll be asking a lot of questions about KMS, keys, logs.
00:00:32 - Maya: great. agenda: scope success criteria, workload numbers, benchmark plan, then deployment mode pros/cons.

00:02:05 - Carlos (SE): quick clarifier — what's your current qps and typical token size?
00:02:12 - Liam: baseline is about 150 reqs per minute during the day, spikes to ~360 for short events; prompts average 110 tokens, responses around 60 tokens, so ~170 tokens total per interaction. imprecision: sometimes called 200 tokens in our rough sheet.
00:02:34 - Tom: and our SREs want p95 under 350ms for synchronous UI calls. Anything above 500ms and product owners start complaining.

00:04:10 - Carlos: ok makes sense. for that profile, hosted can work initially if you accept multi-tenant. Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and predictable throughput; private (VPC/on-prem) addresses the data residency and network egress concerns.
00:04:30 - Priya: what about cost? we have 2 constraints: unit cost per 1k tokens and monthly predictable spend cap.
00:04:40 - Zoe (SA): we typically model cost at both token-cost and committed capacity. we can show a few scenarios — burstable hosted with fallback to cheaper model, or dedicated reserved pool if you want strict latency SLAs.

00:06:01 - Ava: security first — we need customer-managed keys, audit logs retained 1 year, and SSO via SAML. can hosted support that?
00:06:12 - Maya: hosted supports BYOK/KMS integrations and audit logs, but private gives you the fullest control (private control plane, HSM option). hosted can be configured with SAML SSO and per-token logs, though sometimes retention windows vary.
00:06:40 - Priya: can you guarantee no cross-tenant KV cache leakage?
00:06:46 - Carlos: yes — we isolate KV cache per-tenant; there's an isolation guarantee on dedicated and private modes, hosted has strong logical isolation though we recommend dedicated if you're extremely paranoid. note: in some transcriptions our docs said 'K-V cash' which is wrong, but that's the same thing.

00:09:18 - Liam: what benchmarks should we run in the POC? we want to validate latency, throughput, and token cost.
00:09:25 - Carlos: propose three canonical tests: 1) steady-state QPS at 200 reqs/min for 30 minutes, 2) spike test to 400 reqs/min sustained for 5 mins, 3) cold-start + KV cache effectiveness using prefix-heavy prompts. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, token consumption, GPU utilization.
00:09:48 - Priya: can you provide the harness so we can run in our test env and send back results?
00:09:52 - Carlos: yes I'll share a lightweight harness (python + k6 job and a Jenkins pipeline example). link placeholder: https://redwood.mock/harness (will send actual).

00:12:10 - Tom: network topology question: if we go private in our VPC, does Redwood need inbound rules? what's the setup?
00:12:18 - Zoe: for private, we use a customer-peered VPC or private link style peering; the private control plane talks over the customer-managed network. we'll share the ops runbook.
00:12:35 - Tom: any required ports?
00:12:37 - Zoe: yes a small set — SSH not needed typically, HTTPS to a set of endpoints, and gRPC ports for the runtime. we'll document exact CIDR/ports in the checklist.

00:15:03 - Ava: auditability — we need immutable logs, export to our SIEM (Splunk). can you forward logs or do S3 export?
00:15:12 - Maya: both options — hosted can stream logs to your S3 or to our log-forwarder; private can keep logs in your account. we'll include log-forwarder and signed export examples.

00:18:00 - Liam: success criteria from product-side: 1) p95 < 350ms on the steady-state test, 2) error rate < 0.5% under spikes, 3) quality parity vs baseline (human eval on 200 sample outputs).
00:18:15 - Priya: ops success criteria: reproducible benchmark runs, documented rollout steps, and cost model that doesn't exceed $X (internal cap).

00:20:12 - Carlos: on model choices — we can serve open models we verified; we recommend quantized variants for dedicated to reduce cost; hosted can auto-fallback to another compati-ble model if capacity is low.
00:20:30 - Liam: what about warm KV caches? we saw a big perf win in earlier tests.
00:20:36 - Carlos: yes, prefix caching and KV cache warmup can lower p95 by ~30% in our tests; we'll include an experiment to measure that.

00:23:50 - Priya: timeline — we aim to start pilot in 2 weeks and run 6-week pilot. is that feasible?
00:23:58 - Maya: feasible. week 0: SOW + provisioning, week 1: baseline data + benchmark harness run, week 2: Redwood runs hosted and dedicated runs for comparison, weeks 3-4: iteration on config, week 5: security review + final report, week 6: decision.
00:24:20 - Ava: security review timing — we need SOC2 docs and a pen-test summary before week 5.
00:24:28 - Zoe: we'll attach SOC2 & compliance docs and a redacted pen-test whitepaper.

00:26:40 - Tom: what about on-call and incident response during the pilot?
00:26:44 - Maya: Redwood provides an SRE contact for the pilot and a playbook for escalations. dedicated customers can opt into higher SLA with paging.

00:29:10 - Liam: if we choose dedicated, what's the commitment period and scaling options?
00:29:18 - Zoe: dedicated is typically reserved monthly; we offer autoscaling within the reserved pool and short-term burst capacity. contract terms flexible for pilots.

00:31:00 - Priya: tricky one — data residency: we must keep PII within our EU region. hosted region options?
00:31:08 - Maya: hosted supports region pinning for EU-only, but private guarantees that control. we'll map regions and provide a region matrix.

00:34:12 - Carlos: competitor note — you mentioned CloudModelX in RFP; their pitch focuses on cheaper token cost but less observability and heavier ops for private networks. Redwood's angle: predictable economics + observability and smooth migration between modes.
00:34:35 - Priya: cost example request — can you give a modeled cost per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated (with 3 month commit)?
00:34:44 - Maya: yes we'll model several buckets and include a sensitivity table; action: Maya to send pricing table.

00:37:50 - Liam: we also want to validate accuracy/regression. how do you recommend measuring that?
00:37:56 - Carlos: we'd run a 200-sample human eval (blind) comparing current baseline to Redwood-served model; define metrics: exact match, F1, and subjective scores. we'll provide an eval template.

00:40:20 - Priya: legal/procurement cycle — typical enterprise procurement leads to a 4-6 week procurement window after pilot. any fasttracks?
00:40:30 - Maya: pilot-to-contract often short if pilot metrics meet SLA; we can offer pre-approved SOW templates to speed procurement.

00:44:05 - Ava: small thing — encryption at rest key rotation policy?
00:44:10 - Zoe: supported. for hosted customers we can support BYOK with rotation cadence and HSM-backed keys on private. we'll supply a KMS integration doc.

00:47:00 - Carlos: technical note — for benchmarking, do you want us to run both int8 quantized and fp16 runs?
00:47:06 - Priya: yes, include quantized to show cost/latency tradeoffs.

00:50:12 - Maya: recap and next steps: we'll send SOW + pricing + benchmark harness, Carlos will send the scripts, and Galaxy will send traffic samples and the list of 200 eval prompts.
00:50:30 - Liam: agreed. we'll try to get the traffic CSV by Friday.
00:50:36 - Ava: I'll confirm compliance requirements and share the exact retention policy.
00:51:00 - Maya: plan to meet again in one week to confirm SOW and kick off provisioning.

00:55:12 - Tom: random question — what's your approach to rollback if a model regression happens in prod?
00:55:20 - Zoe: we recommend canary rollouts with automatic fallback to an earlier pinned model and alerting tied to evaluation prompts. we'll include that as part of the ops playbook.
00:56:02 - Liam: thanks everyone.
00:56:10 - Maya: thanks, we'll follow up.

End of transcript.

References mentioned: pilot harness link (to be provided), SOW template link (to be provided), SOC2 and KMS docs.
